key_sub: On a number line, further left is smaller, so −9 < −2.
body_html:
How it works

On a number line, numbers to the left are smaller: −9 < −2 < 0 < 3.

Adding a positive number moves right; adding a negative number moves left. Subtracting a positive moves left. Subtracting a negative is the same as adding: 3 − (−5) = 3 + 5 = 8.

To find the difference between two temperatures, subtract the lower from the higher.

Example

Order −4, 2, −11, 0, 7 from smallest to largest.

Furthest left first.

Answer: −11, −4, 0, 2, 7

Example

Work out −4 + (−6).

Start at −4 and move 6 to the left.

Answer: −10

Example

Work out −2 − (−7).

Subtracting −7 is adding 7: −2 + 7.

Answer: 5

Common mistakes

  • Thinking −7 is bigger than −2 because 7 is bigger than 2.
  • Treating 3 − (−5) as 3 − 5. Two minus signs next to each other make a plus.
  • Thinking −4 + (−6) = 10. Adding a negative makes the number smaller.
  • For a temperature difference, subtracting the wrong way: from −8 °C to 5 °C is 13 degrees, not 3.

faq.q: Why does subtracting a negative number give a bigger answer?
faq.a: Taking away a debt leaves you better off. On the number line, 3 − (−5) is the gap from −5 up to 3, which is 8.

faq.q: How do I find the difference between −8 °C and 5 °C?
faq.a: Subtract the lower from the higher: 5 − (−8) = 13 degrees.
